 Ford Recalls 2026 Broncos After Windshield Wiper Arms Risk Falling Off
 MotorBiscuit Saajan Jogia Wed, November 18, 2026 at 4:16 PM UTC Add to Preferred Sources Wed, November 18, 2026 at 4:16 PM UTC The 2026 Ford Bronco has been recalled because the driver side windshield wiper arm may detach, potentially leading to loss of wiper function.
 According to a National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) recall report , 330 units of the Bronco have been affected by an issue relating to the driver side windshield wiper arm nut.
 The report explains that the nut may not have been tightened sufficiently. This could cause the wiper arm to slip on the pivot shaft or detach, thereby compromising wiper function partially or fully.
 The NHTSA states that the defect could reduce visibility when the windshield wiper is needed, increasing the risk of a crash. Explaining the primary cause of the problem, the recall report states:
 Advertisement Advertisement "A mechanical failure occurred in the fastening tool used to tighten the driver side wiper arm nut resulting in inaccurate torque. As a result, affected vehicles may have been assembled with the wiper arm nut insufficiently tightened."
 Ford discovered the issue on September 22, 2026, during a quality audit at its Michigan Assembly Plant, where an inspection revealed insufficient residual torque on the nut securing the driver-side windshield wiper arm of a 2026 Bronco.
 Ford's Critical Concern Review Group (CCRG) began investigating the problem on October 8. After examining engineering specifications and manufacturing torque records, the team determined that although the wipers worked when the vehicles left the factory, the loose fastening could eventually compromise their operation, particularly under additional loads such as snow. The production data also helped Ford identify the potentially affected vehicles.
 The Remedy
 As of October 12, Ford had received no related warranty claims, field reports, customer complaints or Vehicle Owner Questionnaires. The company's Field Review Committee assessed the issue on October 27 and approved a recall. Ford also reported no known accidents or injuries associated with the condition.
 Advertisement Advertisement Ford will contact affected owners through mailed notifications, instructing them to take their vehicles to an authorized Ford or Lincoln dealership.
 During the visit, technicians will examine the operation of the driver-side windshield wiper, check and tighten its retaining nut, and install a replacement wiper arm if necessary. All inspection and repair work associated with this issue will be performed free of charge to vehicle owners.
 Ford had planned to notify its dealerships about the recall on November 6, 2026, and make the affected vehicles searchable by VIN on the same date. Owner notification letters outlining the available remedy are scheduled to be mailed between November 16 and November 20, 2026, meaning the mailing process is already underway and is expected to conclude later this week.
